original_test_intent: Install the approved Windows chipset driver without error, reboot successfully and verify its registry version and Microsoft hardware-compatibility signature.
original_method: Agent validates/stages the exact signed package; qualified operator completes Setup.exe/license/reboot; agent collects post-boot device, registry, catalog and event evidence.
manual_activity: User approves package/license/target/recovery; qualified operator runs Setup.exe, accepts license and supervises the one reboot; agent verifies post-state.
required_inputs: Exact Windows edition/build, platform/chipset and BIOS/firmware support matrix
Approved driver package/version, Setup.exe/catalog hashes and signatures
Expected driver list and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Infinst value or documented equivalent
Restore/recovery image, BitLocker recovery, KVM/OOB and known-event allowlist
safety_requirements: Verify package target, checksum and signature before execution
Capture device/driver/registry/boot baseline and recovery readiness
Supervise installer and one reboot through KVM/OOB
Stop on signature/compatibility ambiguity, installer/device/boot/BitLocker/event/BMC fault or recovery loss
Do not bypass signature enforcement, guess packages or auto-rollback blindly
agent_execution_scope: Validate package/catalog provenance and stage exact artifact
Capture pre/post device, driver, registry, signature and event evidence
Do not accept license, click UI, reboot without approval, disable signing or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Provide qualified operator and own boot/driver recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Linux lsmod/dmesg is inapplicable to the explicitly Windows Setup.exe, Registry Editor and Microsoft catalog-signature workflow.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use approved Windows package/signature, device-manager/driver-store, registry and event tooling around the operator-supervised installer and reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Setup.exe UI/license, completion, reboot, Infinst registry check, signature Criteria and source 5/5 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind installer/catalog provenance to exact platform compatibility, record interactive outcome, then reconcile device state, registry version and catalog signature after one supervised reboot.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds reproducible package identity and rollback evidence without replacing the source UI flow.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Evidence collection may be automated; license/UI/reboot and recovery remain manual.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Chipset packages can update multiple core drivers and registry locations may vary by vendor/version.

project_override_considerations: Project authority must provide the exact signed package and expected registry path/value; Linux module state and a similarly named generic chipset installer are not acceptable substitutes.
expected_evidence: Setup.exe/catalog hashes, signatures, version and license record
Pre/post device-manager, driver-store, provider/version/date and registry state
Complete installer output/exit and one reboot/KVM evidence
Windows System/Application/Setup plus BMC/SEL logs, rollback readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Source Procedure and Criteria consistently define a Windows chipset driver installation; the DeepSeek Linux substitution is rejected rather than treated as competing source authority.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Signed package, compatibility, operator and recovery are supplyable execution prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Corrects the wrong-OS automation and builds a traceable signed Windows driver lifecycle with exact version and boot-recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Loaded Linux modules cannot demonstrate a Windows MSI/Setup package, registry value or catalog signer. A chipset installer may replace boot-critical drivers even if it exits successfully, so validity depends on exact package provenance and post-reboot device/registry/signature/event reconciliation with an available recovery path.
